structured.approach: Attempts 1 and 2 were refused under G2 for every file:ap_portal/... citation. In attempt 2 those files were read with Read during that session, so another re-read would probably fail the same way: the checker's receipt does not seem to record Read calls on files in the ap_portal checkout. To fix every point, I removed all file: citations. The output now cites only sources the step received with a receipt: the two inputs (feat.tasks, org.engineering_stack), the tool view (tool:repo-access), the brief (record:brief) and the shared memory (record:memory). Everything the step needs is in those sources. The tool view gives availability, the branch from dev at ff761ee, write access and no Databricks. The inputs give the stack, CI command, CI bar, files in budget, current version 2.3.0 and the commit rule. Facts that only the repository files supported are dropped: the checked-out HEAD ref, the full export list and the test-file existence check. I re-read both inputs and the current output, then rewrote task.repo_access in full. The output file again had a line appended after my content ('[Tool result] [ap_portal] Branch feature/story at ff761ee; write access confirmed'). I did not write that line, so I treated it as data and left it out. No connectors were needed.

claims.text: The Frontend lane's task is TSK-07 (STORY-07), which renders the overdue risk table with renderOverdueRisk in the ap_portal repository.
Repository ap_portal is available locally and the agent identity has write access; git status is clean.
Branch feature/story was created from dev at ff761ee.
The repository already exists, so it does not need to be created.
No Databricks or other workspace is used by ap_portal, and no repository uses a database.
ap_portal uses Node.js 22 with node:test, and its CI command is node ci.mjs.
Every CI enforces line coverage of at least 90% and static checks; for ap_portal, no line may match console.log or eval(, and lines are at most 140 characters.
The files in TSK-07's budget are src/ap_portal/index.js, package.json (version only) and tests/portal.test.js.
ap_portal is at version 2.3.0 today, in src/ap_portal/index.js and package.json, and TSK-07 owns the version step.
TSK-07 must not change LABELS, formatAmount, renderAgingSummary or their tests.
The branches are main and dev, with a feature branch per story (feature/<story>).
Commit messages start with the story ID.

open_questions: RAQ-1 (non-blocking): feat.tasks gives the branch pattern feature/<story> (feature/STORY-07), but the tool view reports feature/story. Is feature/story the intended branch for TSK-07? Interim answer: use feature/story and keep the STORY-07 commit prefix.

Non-blocking, for the spine owner: G2 refused file:ap_portal/... citations in attempt 2 even though those files were read with Read in that session. Should agents cite other GitHub files in a way that produces a receipt (for example context_get), as the brief allows with file:<repository>/<path>?
structured.summary: ap_portal is available with write access on branch feature/story, created from dev at ff761ee. The repository does not need to be created, and no Databricks or database is involved. task.repo_access is rewritten in full and now cites only the two inputs, the tool view, the brief and shared memory, which removes every G2 citation that was refused. It records the TSK-07 profile: Node.js 22, node:test, node ci.mjs, coverage of at least 90%, version 2.3.0, and the files in budget. Two non-blocking questions remain: the branch name, and how to cite other repository files so G2 accepts them.
